input.question: What was the profession of Henry Moseley?

documents.text: to know Albert, Prince Consort. In 1853 he was presented to a residential canonry in Bristol Cathedral; in 1854 he became a marine biologist and was appointed a research fellow at the Marine Biological Association in 1855. Moseley was elected a Fellow of the Royal Society in February 1839. He was also a corresponding member of the Institute of France, a member of the Council of Marine Research, and vice-president of the Institution of Naval Architects. He died at Olveston 20 January 1872. While at Portsmouth Moseley wrote his first paper, "On measuring the Depth of the Cavities seen on the ocean floor."
